executiveConclusion.primaryReason: The current execution, registration, validation and governance paths are specific to the single P7 hepatic campaign and do not provide a generic, enforced, stable multi-campaign lifecycle.

findings.title: The campaign executor is a one-campaign P7 replay, not a generic executor
evidence: scripts/execute-scientific-campaign.mjs imports the hepatic P7 trace and data directly.
createAutomaticCampaignExecutionTrace requires the selected ID to equal noxia:scientific-campaign:hepatic-imaging:01.
createScientificKnowledgeCatalog exposes only includeCampaignExecutions=true|false and stores exactly one hard-coded execution.
The default selector still reads the frozen P6 catalog.
findings.impact: A second campaign cannot be executed without modifying architecture code, validators and registries.

findings.title: Catalog governance is declarative and bypassable
evidence: The governance functions have no production call site outside tests.
Enrichment authorization checks only node existence and terminal status.
Priority, campaign membership, coverage, dependencies and blockingNodes are ignored.
An unknown operation is treated as SCIENTIFIC_ENRICHMENT and authorized.
A decision for an injected catalog reports the global catalog digest instead of the injected digest.
findings.impact: Scientific enrichment can bypass the official campaign selection contract and can be attributed to the wrong catalog snapshot.

findings.title: Catalog validators do not verify status, readiness and provenance coherence
evidence: READY without sources was accepted in a mutation test.
READY without assertions was accepted in a mutation test.
READY with zero coverage was accepted in a mutation test.
Removing a source reference or assertion reference from node provenance was accepted.
Replacing an EvidenceLink reference with an unknown ID was accepted.
findings.impact: The catalog can advertise readiness while its scientific and provenance records are incomplete or disconnected.

findings.title: Campaign IDs are not bound to the selected node set
evidence: Campaign identity is group slug plus batch ordinal.
Inserting a node changed batch 01 membership without changing its campaignId.
Execution lookup uses campaignId only and skipped the newly inserted node in the mutation test.
findings.impact: Catalog evolution can silently mark a different campaign payload as already executed.

findings.title: Global campaign order is lexicographic, not priority-driven
evidence: The next planned campaign is neuro-oncology at score 68.
Segmentation and T2 mapping both score 70 but appear eighth and ninth.
The nine current campaigns contain 23 priority inversions out of 36 possible pairs.
findings.impact: The Scientific Knowledge Catalog does not currently determine the next campaign according to its own strongest priority score.

findings.title: Candidate and status rules create selection blind spots
evidence: A candidate must have both sourceCoverage<1 and assertionCoverage<1; either gap alone is ignored.
READY, PROJECTED and PUBLISHED are all excluded before coverage gaps are considered.
The current catalog contains 52 PROJECTED nodes with incomplete coverage, including 38 with a source gap and 39 with an assertion gap.
A blocked node remained a campaign candidate in mutation testing.
findings.impact: Incomplete nodes can become permanently invisible to automatic enrichment while blocked nodes can still be scheduled.

findings.title: Dependency governance is unproven and partially unchecked
evidence: The production catalog currently contains zero dependency edges and zero blocking nodes.
Dependency cycles are detected, but prerequisite, blocking-node and successor cycles are not.
Selection and authorization ignore dependencies and blockingNodes.
findings.impact: The system cannot yet demonstrate safe scheduling when real cross-domain dependencies are introduced.

findings.title: P7 validators reject legitimate future growth
evidence: Exact counts for 5 sources, 15 concepts, 22 assertions, 22 links, one execution and nine remaining campaigns are hard-coded.
Catalog node, concept and domain totals are hard-coded.
P6 and P7 digests and the hepatic campaign ID are hard-coded as current-state requirements.
findings.impact: A valid second campaign will require validator rewrites and will otherwise be reported as a regression.

findings.title: Coverage treats unresolved documentary references as scientific source coverage
evidence: sourceCoverage and provenanceReady use sourceCount rather than scientificSourceCount.
114 nodes have source references but zero resolved scientific source records and are still provenanceReady.
22 of those nodes have complete sourceCoverage.
findings.impact: Planning and readiness can overstate scientific provenance for historical or documentary-only nodes.

findings.title: No generic durable execution lifecycle exists
evidence: There is no generic queued, running, failed, retryable, cancelled or resumed campaign state.
There is no lock, lease, attempt number or compare-and-swap against the catalog digest.
The current command rewrites deterministic P7 artifacts rather than executing a selected campaign payload.
findings.impact: Concurrent runs, partial failures and retries cannot be governed safely across hundreds of campaigns.

findings.title: Node planning is fast, but validation and evidence lookup contain superlinear paths
evidence: At 5000 flat domains, median selection was 4.825 ms but graph validation rose to 184.592 ms.
Cycle traversal uses Array.shift and repeated sorting.
Catalog construction performs evidence.find for each EvidenceLink reference.
The exact lookup pattern took 178.447 ms at 10000 links versus 0.961 ms with a Map index.
findings.impact: Tens of thousands of assertions remain plausible but are not validated at industrial scale with the current implementation.

findings.title: The generated catalog is verbose for source-control scale
evidence: The current 250-node JSON is 2.667 MiB, or 11185.9 bytes per node.
A minimal 5000-node synthetic catalog serialized to 27.831 MiB.
The catalog repeats readiness, coverage and fourteen projection evaluations on every node.
findings.impact: Repository churn, reviewability and report size will degrade before computation itself becomes a bottleneck.

findings.title: P7 replay is deterministic but does not revalidate source content
evidence: Twenty local replays produced one value for every compared digest.
All five P7 sources retain official URLs but contentDigest is null.
findings.impact: The system proves deterministic transformation of captured metadata, not byte-level reproducibility of external evidence.

findings.title: Generic node classes exist, but generic campaign ingestion does not
evidence: Modality, Manufacturer, Technology and Biomarker are already valid node types.
Specialty is not a node type and currently needs Domain as a documented fallback.
Adding any real new campaign still requires imports and branches in catalog-builder, validators, execution and reports.
findings.impact: Ontology extension is mostly adequate; operational extension is not plug-in based.

findings.title: P7 reports contain stale phase-specific statements
evidence: The catalog report still lists the P6 HEAD as expectedHead.
It states noCommitPushDeploy=true although P7 is now committed.
Readiness justification still says P6 is the internal planning layer.
findings.impact: Historical reports remain reproducible but can be mistaken for current operational state.
